newsitem.title: GERMANY: German green coffee buyers stay on sidelines.
newsitem.headline: German green coffee buyers stay on sidelines.

text.p: German coffee roasters remain cautious buyers in quiet conditions with both London and New York closed for holidays, traders said on Monday.
"The European industry will not buy Colombians and Central Americans as long as futures and differentials remain at such highs," one trader said.
"Some buyers are taking advantage of Brazilian discounts for July/August shipment coffee," he added.
New York futures raced to new highs last week as a gathering of exporting nationas (ACPC) failed to offer concessions on export mquotas.
New York arabicas last Friday ended at 256.85 cents/lb on July, off 3.45, and at 226.05 cents, off 3.90, on September.
Traders said July's hefty premium over September had little justification.
Certified U.S. coffee stocks were still low -- and U.S. roasters shorter than their European counterparts -- but the premium still appeared to be technically induced.
"The ACPC decision could have boosted the distant months and eased the spot position, but it seems to have done the opposite," another trader said.
"The nearby market should also ease on reports of a good crop quality in Brazil's 1997/98 harvest."
Brazilian farmers indicated initial pickings showed good quality as a result of a long dry spell between mid-March and mid-May.
Brazil differentials for July/August shipment under September futures were at minus 35 cents while the differential versus December arabicas was minus 20 cents.

Nearby cash Brazils last Friday were offered at $217 per 50 kg fob Bremen, off $4 on the week, while Central Americans for more distant months ranged between $299 and $311 and Colombians were at $319.
Vietnam robustas were offered at $92.50 cif.
